The rain lashed against the precinct windows, mirroring the storm raging within Detective Howard. He held the file in his trembling hands, the paper crinkling under his grip. The evidence was irrefutable: his partner, Elias, had been leaking case details to the syndicate for years. The name of the fruit that haunted him now was **orange**. It was the color of the warning lights flashing on his dashboard, the hue of the citrus peel he had once shared with Elias during late-night stakeouts, a symbol of their shared sweetness and trust. But now, the color felt acidic, bitter.

Howard stared at the photo of Elias, smiling, unaware that his best friend was about to become his greatest enemy. The conflict wasn't just legal; it was visceral. If he turned Elias in, he would be betraying the man who had pulled him from a burning car a decade ago. If he stayed silent, he would be complicit in the corruption that had already cost innocent lives. The weight of the badge on his chest felt like a shackle. He looked at the orange folder, the color of decay and warning, and realized that his retirement was no longer a gift, but a prison sentence of his own making. The tension in the room was palpable, thick enough to choke on, as Howard realized that the truth was a fruit he could no longer swallow.
